items.cardTitle: DMV Employer Cost Index 2026
items.cardSub: What one employee costs an employer in statutory taxes, paid leave and wage floors in DC, Maryland and Virginia. Every figure sourced.
items.text:
New: the DMV Employer Cost Index 2026

What does one employee cost an employer in statutory taxes in DC, Maryland and Virginia? We built the answer from primary sources.

- New-employer unemployment insurance: DC 2.90% on $9,000, MD 2.60% on $8,500, VA 2.73% on $8,000
- DC Paid Family Leave: 0.75% of wages, employer-paid
- Maryland FAMLI: 0.90% from 2027

Every figure links to its source. Free, no sign-up.

Source: DC DOES; Maryland Department of Labor; Virginia Employment Commission

Read the index: https://peonomics.com/dmv-employer-cost-index

items.headline: 57 days until Maryland FAMLI contributions begin
items.cardTitle: Maryland FAMLI contributions begin
items.text:
57 days until Maryland FAMLI contributions begin

Starting Jan. 1, 2027, Maryland employers remit FAMLI contributions: 0.90% of wages up to the Social Security wage base ($192,300 in 2027).

Employers with 15 or more employees pay at least half (0.45%) and may withhold the rest from pay. That is up to $865.35 per employee at the wage cap. Smaller employers owe no employer share but must remit what they withhold. Benefits begin by Jan. 3, 2028.

Source: Maryland FAMLI law via Jackson Lewis; SSA 2027 wage base

items.headline: 50 days until the Social Security wage base rises to $192,300
items.cardTitle: Social Security wage base rises
items.text:
50 days until the Social Security wage base rises to $192,300

On Jan. 1, 2027 the cap on wages subject to the 6.2% employer Social Security tax moves from $184,500 to $192,300.

For each employee paid above the cap, the employer's maximum Social Security tax goes from $11,439.00 to $11,922.60: $483.60 more per head.

Source: Social Security Administration

items.cardSub: Average private-sector pay, employer FICA and the employer share of single health coverage at firms under 50 employees.
items.text:
What one employee costs an employer in Vermont, before the extras

In Vermont, three numbers every employer cost starts from:

- Average private-sector pay per job: $66,806 a year (includes part-time jobs)
- Employer Social Security and Medicare on that pay (7.65%): $5,111
- Employer share of single health coverage at firms under 50 employees: $8,838 a year

That is $80,755 before unemployment insurance, workers' comp, retirement, admin or a PEO fee. The Vermont page carries the rest, each figure with its source.

Source: BLS QCEW 2025 annual averages, private; AHRQ MEPS-IC 2025, state tables; 26 U.S.C. 3111

92 days until Virginia's minimum wage reaches $15.00

At 2,080 hours a year, that is $2,600 more per full-time employee at the floor, before payroll taxes.
